name: Flutter
tagline: Build Android and iOS apps from one Dart codebase and ship them to the stores.
why: Flutter is one of the most used cross-platform frameworks in Indian startups and service companies, and campus drives for mobile roles often test Dart, widgets and Android basics.

stages.title: Setup and Dart
stages.goal: Install the tools and get fluent in Dart before widgets.
topics: Install Flutter and run an app on an emulator and a real phone
Git: commit, branch and push to GitHub
stages.build: Ten small Dart console programs: a grade calculator, a discount calculator, a to-do list in memory, and a simple bank account class.
stages.prove: A public GitHub repo with all ten programs and a README.

stages.title: Widgets and layout
stages.goal: Think in widgets and build any screen from a design.
stages.build: Rebuild three real app screens from Figma community files: a login screen, a product list and a profile page, pixel close on phone and tablet.
stages.prove: Screenshots side by side with the designs in your README.

stages.title: Forms, navigation and state
stages.goal: Handle user input, move between screens and keep state sane.
topics: Navigation with go_router and passing data
Local storage with shared_preferences and a database
stages.build: A student records app with add, edit, delete, search and validation, data saved locally, state handled with Riverpod or Bloc.
stages.prove: A short screen recording of the full CRUD flow in the README.
stages.hint: Do not learn both Riverpod and Bloc at first. Check job posts in your city and pick the one they ask for.

stages.title: APIs, Firebase and real data
stages.goal: Talk to servers, handle loading and errors, add sign-in.
topics: HTTP with dio and JSON model classes
stages.build: A news or movie app using a public API with search, pagination, favourites saved offline and Google sign-in.
stages.prove: A release APK link and a demo video.

stages.title: Quality and release
stages.goal: Make it reliable and publish it.
topics: App icons, splash screen and signing
stages.build: Add tests and a CI pipeline to your best app and publish it on the Play Store.
stages.prove: A live Play Store or TestFlight link on your resume.

stages.title: Interview and job ready
stages.goal: Prepare for company exams and interviews.
topics: State management trade-offs in your own words
Two published apps in your portfolio
stages.build: Take every Karmatix Flutter mock test and redo the ones you fail.
stages.prove: Two published apps, a clean GitHub and mock test scores you can talk about.

interview: Widget tree, element tree and render tree
Stateless vs Stateful and when to use each
Keys and why lists need them
How you would make an app work offline
How you reduce rebuilds and jank
note: There is no Flutter certification worth paying for. A published app is the proof employers look for.

name: .NET and C#
tagline: Build web APIs and services with C#, ASP.NET Core and SQL, the way enterprise teams do.
why: .NET is one of the most hired backend stacks in Indian service companies and enterprises, with steady demand for ASP.NET Core, SQL Server and Azure skills.

stages.title: C# and the toolchain
stages.goal: Get fluent in C# and the dotnet CLI.
topics: Install the .NET SDK and use dotnet new, run and test
Types, nullable references and control flow
stages.build: Five console apps: a bank account with transactions, a student grade report, an inventory manager, a file word counter and a CLI to-do list.
stages.prove: A public repo with tests for at least two of them, or the free Foundational C# certification.

stages.title: Modern C# and LINQ
stages.goal: Write the C# that real codebases use.
stages.build: Refactor your console apps with LINQ and async, and add xUnit tests for the core logic.
stages.prove: Green tests in a GitHub Actions run.

stages.title: SQL and EF Core
topics: A local SQL Server or PostgreSQL
EF Core: DbContext, migrations and relationships
Efficient queries: projections and no N+1
stages.build: A library database with books, members and loans, managed through EF Core migrations, with reports written in LINQ and in raw SQL.
stages.prove: A migration history and a README with the schema diagram.

stages.title: ASP.NET Core Web APIs
topics: Validation and error handling with ProblemDetails
stages.build: A student or e-commerce API with auth, validation, pagination, OpenAPI docs and integration tests.
stages.prove: A live API (Azure App Service free tier or Render) with an OpenAPI page.

stages.title: Architecture and production
stages.goal: Structure, ship and run it like a team would.
topics: Clean architecture, and when not to use it
Deploying to Azure with health checks
stages.build: Take the Karmatix production API capstone and extend it with caching, a background job and a deploy pipeline.
stages.prove: AZ-204 if your target companies use Azure, plus a live capstone.

stages.title: Interview and job ready
topics: CLR, garbage collection, value vs reference types
SOLID with examples from your own code
stages.build: Answer the Karmatix .NET interview questions out loud and record yourself once.
stages.prove: Two deployed APIs, tests in CI and confident answers on the common topics.

interview: EF Core tracking and N+1 queries

name: React and Next.js
tagline: Build fast, accessible web apps with React, TypeScript and Next.js.
why: React is the most requested frontend library in Indian job posts, usually with TypeScript and often Next.js.

stages.title: HTML, CSS and JavaScript
stages.goal: Master the platform before the framework.
topics: Modern JavaScript: modules, destructuring, array methods
stages.build: Three Frontend Mentor challenges in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
stages.prove: Live links and a Lighthouse score above 90.

stages.title: React core
topics: useState, useEffect and when you do not need an effect
stages.build: A notes app with search, filters and local storage.
stages.prove: Deployed on Vercel with clean commits.

stages.title: TypeScript and data
stages.goal: Type your app and handle server data properly.
topics: TypeScript types, unions, generics and narrowing
Forms with validation (React Hook Form and Zod)
stages.build: A movie or GitHub explorer app using a public API with caching, pagination and routing.
stages.prove: A README explaining your data flow.

stages.title: Next.js and production
topics: Next.js App Router, layouts and Server Components
Testing with Vitest and Testing Library
Performance: images, bundle size, Core Web Vitals
stages.build: A full-stack Next.js app with auth, a Postgres database and tests.
stages.prove: A live app, CI and a performance before and after write-up.

stages.title: Interview ready
topics: JavaScript internals: closures, this, event loop
Machine coding: build a widget in 60 minutes
stages.build: Do five timed machine coding rounds: autocomplete, modal, tabs, infinite scroll, star rating.
stages.prove: Two portfolio projects and recorded machine coding practice.

name: Node.js
tagline: Build APIs and services in JavaScript or TypeScript on Node.js.
why: Node.js with TypeScript is common in Indian startups, often with Express or NestJS and PostgreSQL or MongoDB.

stages.title: JavaScript and Node basics
topics: The event loop and async patterns
stages.build: A CLI tool and a raw HTTP server that serves JSON.
stages.prove: Both on GitHub with READMEs.

stages.title: APIs with Express
stages.build: A task manager API with users, auth and tests.
stages.prove: An OpenAPI page and a Bruno collection.

stages.title: Databases
topics: MongoDB and when a document store fits
stages.build: Move the task API to Postgres with Prisma migrations and seed data.
stages.prove: A schema diagram and migration history.

stages.title: TypeScript, NestJS and production
topics: Caching with Redis and rate limiting
stages.build: Rebuild the API in NestJS with caching, a job queue and Docker, deployed with CI.
stages.prove: A live API and a short architecture write-up.

stages.title: Interview ready
topics: Security: OWASP top risks in APIs
stages.build: Design and explain two systems: a URL shortener and a chat service.
stages.prove: Two deployed APIs and a design doc.

name: Python backend
tagline: Build APIs and services with Python, Django or FastAPI and PostgreSQL.
why: Python backends with Django or FastAPI are common in Indian startups and in AI product teams that need to serve models.

stages.title: Python fundamentals
topics: Data types, control flow and functions
Modules, virtual environments and pip or uv
stages.build: Automate one real task: rename files, clean a spreadsheet or scrape a page.
stages.prove: CS50P final project on GitHub.

stages.title: Web basics and Django
topics: HTTP, HTML forms and REST basics
Django models, views, templates and admin
stages.build: A blog or clinic app with users, admin and a REST API.
stages.prove: Deployed with a live link.

stages.title: FastAPI and async
topics: FastAPI routes, Pydantic models and dependency injection
stages.build: An API with auth, Postgres and auto-generated docs.
stages.prove: An OpenAPI page and tests.

stages.title: Testing and production
topics: Caching with Redis and background tasks with Celery or RQ
stages.build: Add tests, Docker, CI and a background job to your FastAPI app and deploy it.
stages.prove: A green pipeline and a live URL.

stages.title: Interview ready
stages.build: Solve 50 interview problems in Python and do one CodeCrafters challenge.
stages.prove: Two deployed APIs and a design write-up.

name: Java and Spring Boot
tagline: Build enterprise APIs with modern Java, Spring Boot and SQL.
why: Java with Spring Boot is the most hired backend stack in Indian service companies, banks and large product companies.

stages.title: Modern Java
stages.goal: Learn Java as it is written today.
topics: Syntax, types, control flow and methods
Records, sealed types and pattern matching
stages.build: Finish the Helsinki MOOC exercises for parts 1 to 7.
stages.prove: A GitHub repo of your solutions.

stages.title: Spring Boot APIs
stages.goal: Build REST APIs the Spring way.
topics: REST controllers, validation and exception handling
stages.build: An employee or library management API with validation and tests.
stages.prove: An OpenAPI page and green tests.

stages.title: Data and security
stages.build: Add a database, migrations and JWT auth to your API.
stages.prove: A schema diagram and auth flow write-up.

stages.title: Production and microservices
stages.goal: Run Spring apps like teams do.
topics: Messaging with Kafka or RabbitMQ basics
Microservices and when not to use them
stages.build: Split one feature into a separate service that talks over a queue, all in Docker Compose.
stages.prove: A live deployment and an architecture diagram.

stages.title: Interview ready
stages.build: Solve 100 problems in Java across the main patterns.
stages.prove: Two deployed projects and confident answers on the common topics.

name: Android with Kotlin
tagline: Build native Android apps with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.
why: India is an Android-first market, so native Android skills stay in steady demand at product companies and fintech.

stages.title: Kotlin
topics: Types, null safety and control flow
Classes, data classes and sealed classes
stages.build: Kotlin Koans plus five small console programs.
stages.prove: A GitHub repo with your solutions.

stages.title: Compose UI
topics: Layouts, lists and theming with Material 3
stages.build: Finish Android Basics with Compose and build a multi-screen app.
stages.prove: Screenshots and code on GitHub.

stages.title: Data and architecture
topics: Recommended architecture: UI, domain and data layers
stages.build: A news or expense app with Room, an API, offline support and Hilt.
stages.prove: An architecture diagram in the README.

stages.title: Quality and release
stages.goal: Test and ship to the Play Store.
topics: Signing, app bundles and Play Console
stages.build: Publish your app on the Play Store with tests and CI.
stages.prove: A Play Store link.

stages.title: Interview ready
stages.build: Explain your published app's architecture and trade-offs out loud.
stages.prove: A published app and interview notes.

note: Google retired its Associate Android Developer certification. A Play Store app is the proof that counts.

name: React Native
tagline: Build iOS and Android apps with React and Expo.
why: React Native is a natural move for React developers and is used by many Indian startups for their first apps.

stages.title: React and JavaScript
stages.goal: Have the React basics in place.
topics: React components, props, state and hooks
stages.build: A small React web app with state and a public API.
stages.prove: A live link.

stages.title: Expo and core components
topics: View, Text, Image, FlatList and Pressable
stages.build: A recipe or notes app with three screens and navigation.
stages.prove: A demo video.

stages.title: Data, storage and native features
topics: Camera, location and notifications with Expo modules
Auth with Firebase or a backend
stages.build: An app with sign-in, cloud data, notifications and offline support.
stages.prove: A test account for reviewers.

stages.title: Release
stages.build: Publish on Play Store or TestFlight with EAS.
stages.prove: A store link.

interview: How the React Native bridge and new architecture work

name: Go
tagline: Build fast, simple services and cloud tooling with Go.
why: Go runs most cloud infrastructure (Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform) and is popular in fintech and high-scale Indian product companies.

stages.title: Go basics
stages.build: Three CLI tools: a file organiser, a word counter and a JSON pretty printer.
stages.prove: A GitHub repo with tests.

stages.title: Web services
stages.goal: Build HTTP APIs with the standard library.
topics: Database access with database/sql or pgx
stages.build: A REST API with Postgres, middleware and tests, using only the standard library and a router.
stages.prove: An OpenAPI page and tests.

stages.title: Concurrency and production
stages.goal: Write safe concurrent code and ship it.
topics: Worker pools, select and sync primitives
stages.build: Add a concurrent worker pool and Docker deployment, then do one CodeCrafters challenge in Go.
stages.prove: A live service and a completed challenge.
